newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper sets sights on $2,440, year's hig.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper sets sights on $2,440, year's hig.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper, having established a toehold above $2,400 per tonne, is now aiming to extend its gains to this year's high of $2,440, technical analysts said.
Aluminium's charts also look friendly, but a sticky stretch of resistance all the way up to $1,700 means the market may need to consolidate or correct slightly before conquering the upside.
COPPER - A rise in bullish sentiment in the copper market, coupled with a brighter technical picture, more than likely spell more near-term gains, analysts said.
Monday's breach of the recent high of $2,407 a tonne had set the next target at $2,440, the year's high from March 7.
"The technical indicators are rising in confirmation of the market's recent strength with good support now available at $2,400 and extending towards $2,375," brokers Brandeis said in a commentary.
"The market now eyes the next band of resistance at $2,420 and this year's high at $2,440."
One the downside, $2,370 was important support, said Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading Ltd.
However, LME stocks would also help set the tone in the market, analysts sand traders said.
Inventories saw a small rise of 525 tonnes on Tuesday morning after declining on Monday.
At 0800 GMT three months copper was indicated at $2,412/15, compared to Monday's late close of $2,416/18.
ALUMINIUM - The market was displaying difficulty breaching a band of historic resistance stretching up to $1,700, suggesting it might need to pause before moving foward, analysts said.
"Although still technically positive the market may need a further consolidation period to strenghten its upward thrust," brokers Gerald said in a commentary.
On the downside, a break below $1,667 could target $1,648 or lower, said Creates of AMT.
But steadily declining LME stocks, which fell by 3,150 tonnes on Tuesday, would continue to underpin the market.
At 0800 GMT three months aluminium was indicated at $1,666/69 per tonne, compared with Monday's late close of $1,670/73.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
